what: Accident reported between two cars stopped in a queue (fixed)
why: Identity switch: the track jumped from one queued car to the car behind it, which read as a sudden move and stop. The tracker's fallback gate now scales with the track's own motion, and collision rules reject jumping boxes.

what: Accident reported between a bus and a car on the far road (fixed)
why: Perspective: the boxes overlap on screen but the vehicles are metres apart. Distances are now capped by the smaller party's size, a turn is no impact without a loss of speed, and the far road is excluded.

what: Illegal turn reported for a distant car (fixed)
why: Tracking noise on a small box looked like a rarely seen movement. Illegal turns now need a drawn no-turn rule; turn rules require a reliable track.

what: Jaywalking reported for a pedestrian walking along the crosswalk (fixed)
why: The learned crossing area missed the less used end of the zebra. The crosswalks are now traced, with a two-body-width margin.

what: Red light reported for cars flowing on green (fixed)
why: One car waiting at the line (probably to turn) was taken as proof of red. Without a visible light two waiting cars are needed, and a steady stream of crossings means green.

what: Danger alarm while one car passes in front of another (open)
why: Without depth, boxes that overlap on screen are predicted to meet. Part B now needs a head-on approach on two consecutive frames, which removed 9 of 10 such alarms in this video; this one remains.
